callee_census.other_sites_note: census only; the other nine sites' enclosing functions are not modelled here

caller_census.method: full .text scan for e8 rel32 calls and e9 rel32 jumps to 0x514bc60

container_chain.entry_first_qword: address of a slot; the slot's content is the callee argument (the loop loads [cursor], then [that value], before the call)

notes: Instruction-level detail lives only in the raw objdump excerpts; this JSON holds semantic records only.
The endbr64 at 0x514bc60 and the endbr64 at 0x5032f40 are genuine instructions in the target binary, not placeholders; the nopl at 0x514bc91 is genuine alignment padding before the loop head.
The callee has no int3 padding: its FDE ends at 0x5032f4d and the following bytes belong to another function's tail, so padding_bytes is 0, not a missing record.
The entry's own FDE range ends at 0x514bcc3; the 13 int3 bytes to the next FDE at 0x514bcd0 are padding, verified byte-for-byte.
The callee is shared: nine other direct call sites use it besides this entry. This packet claims the range-sum loop, not exclusive ownership of the callee.
The container chain ([rdi+0x788], then +0x30, then the +0xb18/+0xb20 range) is transliterated, not typed: no source-level type name is claimed for any link.
objdump's nearest-symbol annotations are explicitly not claimed as symbol names.

rule.accumulation: plain 64-bit wrapping add (add %rax,%rbp); no saturation, no overflow check
rule.arguments: rdi = input object, rsi = out pointer
rule.empty_range: begin == end skips the loop via the je at 0x514bc8f; [rsi] = 0, return 1
rule.per_entry: contribution = [callee_argument + 0x10] + 62, where callee_argument = the qword stored at the address held in entry + 0x0 (the loop loads [cursor] into rax, then [rax] into rdi, before the call)
rule.result: return 1 always; [rsi] = sum over the range, 0 for an empty range
